## Description

Also measure the cost of the hash-chain trigger (MDV-P0-036): AccessLogTests seeds 150,000 audit events through the per-row chain trigger; locally that takes seconds but on a shared CI runner it exceeded Npgsql's 30 s default (fixed for the tests with a 300 s command timeout). Record the rows-per-second of an audit insert and of a bulk load, and decide whether bulk loads of ledgered tables need a batch path before the P5 legacy migration.
The P1-037 budgets were measured on SQL Server. Re-run the booking, check-in and calendar load tests on Postgres, confirm 0 double bookings in 100 parallel bookings, and update the budgets and docs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given 100 parallel bookings for one slot, when they run, then exactly one succeeds.
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the desk load profile, when it runs, then the p95 budgets in load-testing.md still hold or are updated with evidence.
- [ ] **AC3.** Given the hash-chain trigger, when 150,000 audit events are inserted on the CI runner, then the rows per second are recorded in load-testing.md and the AccessLog 30-day budget test passes without a raised timeout, or the batch path decision is recorded.

## Definition of Done

All acceptance criteria above, **plus** the cross-cutting X1–X8 checklist in [docs/05-delivery](../../README.md#definition-of-done-every-ticket).
